summary: The note describes the European Rapid Operational Force (EUROFOR), a multinational rapid reaction force made up of units from Italy, France, Portugal and Spain. It had a permanent staff able to command operations up to Light Division size and was formed in Lisbon in May 1995, reporting directly to the Western European Union. Its tasks covered Petersberg missions such as humanitarian, peacekeeping and peace enforcement operations. After the WEU merged into the European Union, it became part of the Common Security and Defence Policy, was turned into an EU Battlegroup on standby from 1 July to 31 December 2011, and was dissolved on 2 July 2012.
one_line: EUROFOR was a multinational EU rapid reaction force from Italy, France, Portugal and Spain, formed in 1995 and dissolved in 2012.
key_facts: The European Rapid Operational Force (EUROFOR) was a multinational rapid reaction force composed of forces from four states of the European Union: Italy, France, Portugal and Spain.
EUROFOR had a permanent staff capable of commanding operations involving commitments of up to a Light Division in size.
EUROFOR was formed in May 1995 in Lisbon.
EUROFOR was answerable directly to the Western European Union (WEU).
EUROFOR was tasked with performing Petersberg tasks, including humanitarian, peacekeeping and peace enforcement missions.
With the merger of several WEU elements into the European Union, EUROFOR had by and large become part of the Common Security and Defence Policy.
EUROFOR was eventually transformed into an EU Battlegroup.
EUROFOR was on standby as an EU Battlegroup from 1 July until 31 December 2011.
